body:
## Pull request overview

This PR introduces Phase 1 of the plugin modularization effort for ObjectUI, addressing the lack of plugin identity, lifecycle hooks, and runtime install/uninstall capability for example apps. It formalizes a plugin class standard (`AppMetadataPlugin` interface + `AppPluginContext`), adds `install()`/`uninstall()` to `PluginSystem`, refactors the three example apps (CRM, Todo, Kitchen Sink) into proper plugin classes, and streamlines the root `objectstack.config.ts` using `getConfig()` + `flatMap()`.

**Changes:**
- New `AppMetadataPlugin` and `AppPluginContext` interfaces added to `@object-ui/types` with full lifecycle hooks (`init/start/stop/getConfig`)
- `PluginSystem.install()`/`uninstall()` convenience API added to `@object-ui/core`, with 5 new tests
- Example apps (`CRM`, `Todo`, `KitchenSink`) converted to plugin classes; root config refactored to collect configs via `getConfig()` + `flatMap()`

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 11 out of 11 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `packages/types/src/plugin-scope.ts` | Adds `AppPluginContext` and `AppMetadataPlugin` interfaces |
| `packages/types/src/index.ts` | Re-exports the two new types from plugin-scope |
| `packages/core/src/registry/PluginSystem.ts` | Adds `install()`/`uninstall()` methods wrapping `loadPlugin`/`unloadPlugin` |
| `packages/core/src/registry/__tests__/PluginSystem.test.ts` | 5 new tests for install/uninstall lifecycle |
| `objectstack.config.ts` | Replaces manual config spread with plugin-class-based `getConfig()` + `flatMap()` |
| `examples/crm/plugin.ts` | Adds `stop()` and `getConfig()`, types `ctx` as `AppPluginContext` |
| `examples/todo/plugin.ts` | New `TodoPlugin` class with full lifecycle |
| `examples/todo/package.json` | Adds `./plugin` export entry |
| `examples/kitchen-sink/plugin.ts` | New `KitchenSinkPlugin` class with full lifecycle |
| `examples/kitchen-sink/package.json` | Adds `./plugin` export entry |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Adds P2.6 tracking Phases 1–4 of plugin modularization |
</details>

The `getConfig()` method is typed as returning `any`, which bypasses TypeScript's type-checking. Since the return value is always a result of `defineStack()`, the return type should use the concrete type returned by that function (such as `ReturnType<typeof import('@objectstack/spec').defineStack>` or the relevant `ObjectStack` type) to preserve type safety. The codebase's coding guidelines explicitly forbid the use of `any`. Using `any` here propagates into `objectstack.config.ts` where all `allConfigs` access is also typed as `any`, silently hiding potential schema shape errors.

If `install()` is called concurrently with the same plugin name (e.g., two awaited calls in parallel), both could pass the `this.loaded.has(plugin.name)` guard before either one marks the plugin as loaded (since the guard is checked before `await plugin.init()`, which yields control). This could result in `init()` being called twice. The "should not install the same plugin twice" test only covers sequential calls. For the async case, a promise-based lock or an in-progress tracking `Set` should be used. Even if concurrent install is not a current use case, the current test does not protect against a subtle regression.

The ROADMAP entry says "Define `PluginContext` interface for lifecycle hook context (logger, kernel)" but the actual interface introduced in this PR is named `AppPluginContext` (not `PluginContext`). `PluginContext` is the name already exported from `@objectstack/spec`. The roadmap item should read "Define `AppPluginContext` interface for lifecycle hook context (logger, kernel)".
```suggestion
- [x] Define `AppPluginContext` interface for lifecycle hook context (logger, kernel)
```

The `TodoPlugin` class does not declare `implements AppMetadataPlugin`, even though the interface's own JSDoc example (`@example` block in `plugin-scope.ts`) shows classes using this declaration. Without it, TypeScript won't emit a compile error if the class diverges from the interface contract in a future refactor. Adding `implements AppMetadataPlugin` makes the structural constraint explicit and self-documenting.

Without it, TypeScript won't emit a compile error if the class diverges from the interface contract in a future refactor. Adding `implements AppMetadataPlugin` makes the structural constraint explicit and self-documenting.

The interface's own JSDoc example (`@example` block in `plugin-scope.ts`) shows classes using this declaration. Without it, TypeScript won't emit a compile error if the class diverges from the interface contract in a future refactor.
